rca of the issue: Trailer 'Video unavailable' fallback miss: CleanTrailer.tsx relies on YouTube postMessage onError events. When YouTube's own embed player renders the 'Video unavailable / This content isn't available' inline UI (common for IP-blocked or region-restricted embeds), it does NOT dispatch an onError postMessage — the iframe is technically 'playing' the error card. Result: our fallback (trailer-tab-player-unavailable) never mounts, and the user sees YouTube's error UI behind our custom controls. Mitigation: (a) call YouTube oEmbed API to pre-check the videoId before instantiating the iframe, or (b) use YT.PlayerState error codes via IFrame API onStateChange (2,5,100,101,150) instead of postMessage, or (c) use a MutationObserver / timeout — if no 'playing' state within N seconds after user Start, switch to fallback.
